title: Decompression With or Without Fusion Across Subgroups With Degenerative Lumbar Spondylolisthesis : A Target Trial Emulation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Randomized trials have shown limited benefits and increased risks of adding spinal fusion surgery to decompression for degenerative spondylolisthesis. Decompression with fusion has increasingly been used in the United States. OBJECTIVE: To examine the comparative effectiveness of decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for patient subgroups. DESIGN: Cohort study using the target trial framework. SETTING: Norwegian Registry for Spine Surgery and nested NORDSTEN-DS (Norwegian degenerative spondylolisthesis and spinal stenosis) randomized trial. PATIENTS: Adults aged 18 to 80 years with lumbar degenerative spondylolisthesis and symptomatic back or leg pain lasting at least 3 months. INTERVENTION: Lumbar spinal decompression surgery with fusion versus lumbar spinal decompression surgery alone. MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcomes were Oswestry Disability Index (ODI) score and reoperation at 12 months. Linear regression models with inverse probability weighting to control for baseline confounding were used to obtain effect estimates with 95% CIs for decompression with fusion versus decompression alone for prespecified subgroups, including sex, age, smoking, body mass index (BMI), back pain intensity, and American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) grade. RESULTS: Of 2252 patients, 236 were in the NORDSTEN-DS randomized trial. The mean age was 66 years, and 1576 (70%) women were included. A total of 1446 patients had decompression alone, and 806 had decompression with fusion; respective unadjusted baseline ODI scores were 38.9 (SD, 14.9) and 41.4 (SD, 14.7). At 12 months, the ODI score was 22.3 (95% CI, 15.5 to 29.1) for decompression alone and 20.0 (CI, 13.9 to 26.2) for decompression with fusion; the mean difference was 2.2 (CI, -1.6 to 6.1). In exploratory analyses, the ODI score was worse for decompression with fusion for men with BMI of 30 kg/m2 or higher. Reoperation risk at 12 months did not differ. LIMITATION: Possible residual confounding. CONCLUSION: Patient subgroups did not have differential effects from the addition of fusion to decompression at 12 months. PRIMARY FUNDING SOURCE: Research Council of Norway.

title: A randomized comparison of comprehensive weight loss intervention vs. usual care on recurrences of atrial fibrillation in obese patients after catheter ablation: HOBIT-AF trial.
abstract: AIMS: Obesity is one of the strongest risk factors for the development of atrial fibrillation (AF), and its reduction is associated with the alleviation of AF burden. The HOBIT-AF study aimed to evaluate the impact of complex weight loss interventions on AF recurrence rate in obese individuals after catheter ablation (CA). METHODS AND RESULTS: The HOBIT-AF was a randomized controlled trial with a 15-month treatment period (3-18 months post CA) involving complex weight-reducing interventions in the active arm. The primary outcome was the change in AF/atrial tachycardia (AT) burden assessed from baseline and the final 14-day Holter monitoring. A total of 167 individuals (aged 59 years, body mass index of 35.6 kg/m2) were randomized into the active (n = 85) and control group (n = 82). At the end of the treatment period, a mean reduction of 6.8 ± 7.0% of the initial body weight accompanied by improvement of metabolic parameters was achieved in the active group. The AF/AT burden change was 0.6 ± 2.5% (95% CI: -4.2-5.5%) in the active group and -0.9 ± 1.8% (95% CI: -4.5-3.0%) in the control group. The AF/AT recurrence-free survival during the 3-18-month follow-up period was comparable between groups (70.4% vs. 69.6%). CONCLUSION: HOBIT-AF trial showed that despite the beneficial effect of body weight reduction on metabolic profile of obese patients with predominantly paroxysmal AF after CA, no reduction in AF/AT recurrence was observed in comparison with control patients. This may be likely due to low AF burden after previous CA, limiting further improvement.

title: Vascular Phenotypes and Recurrent Arterial Events After Nontraumatic Cervical Artery Dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Nontraumatic cervical artery dissection (CeAD) is often approached as a localized cervicocranial vascular disorder, although overlap with fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) and other arteriopathies suggests broader vascular disease. OBJECTIVES: The objectives of the study was to determine whether head-to-pelvis imaging identifies clinically meaningful vascular phenotypes after nontraumatic CeAD and whether these phenotypes are associated with recurrent arterial events. METHODS: Consecutive adults with CeAD evaluated in an institutional vascular medicine clinic underwent head-to-pelvis computed tomography and/or magnetic resonance angiography. Patients were classified as isolated CeAD, FMD-associated CeAD (FMD-CeAD), or multiple artery aneurysm and dissection without FMD (MAAD). Outcomes were recurrent CeAD and incident extracervical artery dissection. RESULTS: Among 315 patients, 136 (43.2%) had isolated CeAD, 100 (31.7%) had FMD-CeAD, and 79 (25.1%) had MAAD-CeAD. Overall, 179 patients (56.8%) had systemic vascular abnormalities, and 125 (39.7%) had findings below the neck. Recurrent CeAD was most frequent in isolated CeAD. Incident extracervical artery dissection occurred most frequently in MAAD-CeAD. Isolated CeAD was associated with recurrent CeAD compared with FMD-CeAD (HR: 3.26; 95% CI: 1.43 to 7.43). Among patients with FMD-CeAD or MAAD-CeAD, MAAD-CeAD was associated with incident extracervical artery dissection after adjustment for age at index CeAD (HR: 3.75; 95% CI: 1.17-12.00; P = 0.026), with similar results after additional adjustment for baseline aneurysm. CONCLUSIONS: Head-to-pelvis imaging identified frequent extracervical vascular abnormalities in patients with CeAD and phenotypes with distinct recurrent-event patterns. These findings support a cardiovascular arteriopathy framework for CeAD and provide a rationale for prospective studies of phenotype-guided imaging, genetic evaluation, counseling, and surveillance.

title: Cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (DAPT-SHOCK-AMI): a randomised, double-blind trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) can compromise the administration and absorption of oral P2Y12 inhibitors and carries high ischaemic and mortality risks. This trial assessed whether intravenous cangrelor was non-inferior to crushed oral ticagrelor for short-term clinical outcomes and whether it provided faster and more consistent platelet inhibition in patients with AMI-CS. METHODS: DAPT-SHOCK-AMI was a double-blind trial conducted at 29 hospitals across five European countries (Czech Republic, France, Germany, Poland, and Slovakia). Patients older than 18 years with AMI-CS were randomly assigned (1:1 ratio, stratified by centre, age, sex, presence or absence of ST-segment elevation, and mechanical ventilation) to cangrelor (30 μg/kg bolus followed by an infusion of 4 μg/kg per min for at least 2 h) or crushed ticagrelor (180 mg loading dose). The primary laboratory endpoint was a platelet reactivity index of less than 50% at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. The primary clinical endpoint was death, myocardial infarction, or ischaemic stroke at 30 days. The primary clinical endpoint was analysed for non-inferiority with a prespecified margin of 1 percentage point among all randomly assigned patients who received study treatment. The study is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03551964) and EudraCT (2018-002161-19); recruitment and 1-year follow-up are complete, and 5-year follow-up is ongoing. FINDINGS: Between Aug 1, 2018, and Jan 19, 2024, 605 patients (137 [23%] were female) were randomly assigned to cangrelor (n=298) or ticagrelor (n=307); no surviving patients were lost to the 1-year follow-up. The primary laboratory endpoint was analysed in 56 (19%) patients in the cangrelor group and 68 (22%) in the ticagrelor group, and was achieved in 56 (100%) of 56 patients receiving cangrelor and 15 (22%) of 68 receiving ticagrelor (p<0·0001). The 30-day primary clinical endpoint occurred in 112 (38%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 126 (41%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor; non-inferiority was not demonstrated (difference -4 percentage points [90% CI -10 to 3]; Pnon-inferiority=0·13). Major bleeding at 30 days occurred in 19 (6%) of 298 patients receiving cangrelor and 16 (5%) of 307 receiving ticagrelor. INTERPRETATION: To our knowledge, this is the first randomised trial to compare P2Y12 inhibitor strategies specifically in patients with AMI-CS. Cangrelor achieved effective platelet inhibition more frequently than crushed ticagrelor at the end of primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Non-inferiority of cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor was not demonstrated for the primary 30-day clinical endpoint. These trial findings can inform future trials of P2Y12 inhibition strategies in patients with AMI-CS. FUNDING: Czech Republic Ministry of Health, Charles University (Czech Republic), and NextGenerationEU.

title: CD36 Gates Nocturnal Hypertension via the Renal AMPK/HDAC5/PER1 Axis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Nocturnal hypertension is a strong predictor of cardio-cerebrovascular disease, yet its underlying mechanisms remain largely unknown. In this study, we identified CD36 as a key regulator of blood pressure (BP) rhythms and as a gatekeeper of nocturnal hypertension. Its deficiency disrupts circadian BP rhythms. METHODS: We continuously monitored 48-hour BP using telemetry in CD36 global knockout mice and renal proximal tubule-specific CD36 knockout mice. We also collected serum samples and ambulatory BP monitoring data from patients with nocturnal hypertension to assess the relationship between CD36 expression and nocturnal hypertension. A comprehensive screening of various factors affecting BP and circadian rhythms was conducted to explore the molecular mechanisms. RESULTS: Our telemetry data revealed significantly elevated BP during the daytime (inactive period) in both CD36 global knockout and renal proximal tubule-specific knockout mice compared with their control counterparts. Furthermore, levels of platelet CD36 were negatively correlated with the severity of nocturnal hypertension in humans. Mechanistically, CD36 modulates BP rhythms through the AMPK (AMP-activated protein kinase)/HDAC5 (histone deacetylase 5)/PER1 pathway: its deficiency activates phosphorylated AMPK, leading to the dissociation of the HDAC5-PER1 complex, enhancing PER1 nuclear accumulation, and desynchronizing the oscillations of intrarenal renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system genes and clock-controlled genes, ultimately disrupting BP rhythm. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight CD36 as a critical integrator that links renal clocks to BP homeostasis, establishing it as a potential predictor and therapeutic target for nocturnal hypertension.

title: Prediction of Bailout Mechanical Circulatory Support Use for Hemodynamic Collapse During PCI: The ORACLE Score.
abstract: Background: Bailout mechanical circulatory support (MCS) may be used in the setting of intraprocedural hemodynamic collapse during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). We developed and externally validated a simple risk prediction model for bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI. Methods: Consecutive patients undergoing PCI at a tertiary hospital between 2018 and 2025 were included in the derivation cohort (n=6,931), after excluding cases of salvage PCI and procedures performed with pre-existing or prophylactic MCS. The primary endpoint was bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse. A multivariable Firth logistic regression model was developed, internally validated, and translated into a simplified integer-based risk score (ORACLE). External validation was performed in 214,877 PCIs from the Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan Cardiovascular Consortium (BMC2) registry. Results: The incidence of bailout MCS was 1.4% in the derivation cohort. Six variables (non-elective presentation, systolic blood pressure, chronic heart failure, prior PCI, rotational/orbital atherectomy, and left main PCI) independently predicted the primary endpoint. The regression model demonstrated good discrimination both in the derivation (area under the curve [AUC] 0.817; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.774-0.860) and external validation (AUC 0.761; 95% CI 0.753-0.770) cohorts. The simplified ORACLE score preserved most of the discriminatory performance of the full model (AUC 0.791 in the derivation cohort and 0.718 in the external validation cohort) and effectively stratified patients, with observed bailout MCS rates ranging from 0.4% in the low-risk category to 8.7% in the high-risk group, with similar findings in the external validation cohort. Discrimination was consistent across clinically relevant subgroups. Negative predictive value was >99% in both the derivation and external validation cohorts. Conclusions:: ORACLE is a simple score to estimate the risk of bailout MCS use for hemodynamic collapse during PCI, which may support preprocedural risk assessment.

title: The interplay of fibrinogen and lipoprotein(a) with 20-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk: a path analysis within the ATTICA study (2002-2022).
abstract: AIMS: Elevated levels of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] and fibrinogen are known risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), and their combined elevation in high-risk individuals may amplify risk. However, the long-term impact of this combination on ASCVD incidence in a primary prevention setting remains unclear. This study sought to examine the association between the combination of Lp(a) and fibrinogen with long-term ASCVD risk, in apparently healthy adults from the general population. METHODS AND RESULTS: A cohort of 3042 CVD-free adults residing in greater Athens, Greece, was recruited in 2002. A 20-year follow-up was conducted in 2022, comprising n = 2169 participants, of which n = 1988 had complete data for cardiovascular disease incidence. Participants were divided into four groups, using a recommended threshold of 30 mg/dL for Lp(a) and the median value of 303 mg/dL for fibrinogen. In the overall cohort, fibrinogen was associated with higher ASCVD risk [hazard ratio (HR) per 10 mg/dL: 1.040, 95%CI:1.009-1.072]. Upon stratification by Lp(a) levels, the significant association was retained and amplified only in individuals with elevated Lp(a) levels (HR 1.083, 95%CI:1.009-1.162) (P for interaction=0.041). Participants with both elevated Lp(a) and fibrinogen levels demonstrated the highest 20-year ASCVD risk (HR 1.904, 95%CI [1.023, 3.547]). Path analysis revealed a mediating role of fibrinogen in the inflammation [i.e. interleukin-6 (IL-6)]-ASCVD risk association, which become more pronounced at higher Lp(a) concentrations. CONCLUSION: In this general population study, elevated levels of Lp(a) and fibrinogen jointly conferred a higher long-term risk of ASCVD than either marker alone, potentially through the complex involvement of inflammation.

title: Cardiac electrophysiology procedures must be performed exclusively by trained electrophysiologists: A statement from the Heart Rhythm Society and Heart Rhythm Advocates.
abstract: The exponential growth of clinical cardiac electrophysiology (CCEP) as a subspecialty has created an important unresolved question in contemporary cardiovascular medicine: Who is qualified to perform electrophysiology (EP) procedures? As nonelectrophysiologists increasingly perform procedures that require the nuanced expertise of a trained or board-certified CCEP (eg, permanent pacemaker implantation, implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation, cardiac resynchronization therapy, and transvenous lead extraction), the consequences for patient safety, procedural outcomes, and health system efficiency have become impossible to ignore. This article presents a comprehensive, evidence-based argument that cardiac EP procedures must be performed exclusively by physicians who have completed accredited fellowship training in CCEP. We draw upon peer-reviewed outcome data, guideline-derived training standards from the Heart Rhythm Society, the American College of Cardiology, and American Heart Association, including the newly published 2026 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association/Heart Rhythm Society Advanced Training Statement on Clinical Cardiac Electrophysiology, as well as registry analyses spanning hundreds of thousands of patients to substantiate our position. The risks associated with suboptimal operator training are not theoretical; they are measurable, costly, and potentially fatal. The evidence presented demonstrates that operator specialization in EP is among the most powerful independent predictors of procedural safety and long-term outcomes and can be as important as institutional volume in many analyses. We call upon hospital credentialing committees, national medical societies, payers, regulatory bodies, and policymakers worldwide to establish and enforce a definitive standard: only trained CCEPs should implant and manage cardiac implantable electronic devices, perform catheter ablation procedures, execute transvenous lead extraction, and conduct formal EP studies.

title: Global, regional and national burden of cervical cancer in 1990-2023 with forecasts to 2050: a Global Burden of Disease study.
abstract: Although highly preventable, cervical cancer remains one of the most common malignancies among women worldwide. As part of the Global Burden of Disease study, we estimated cervical cancer incidence, mortality and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, with forecasts to 2050. In 2023, 887,000 new cases (95% uncertainty interval 682,000-1,170,000), 369,000 deaths (292,000-475,000) and 13.3 million DALYs (10.1-17.4) were estimated globally. Age-standardized incidence rate (ASIR) and age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) were more than four and seven times higher in low- versus high-income countries. Between 1990 and 2023, global ASIR was largely stable (-0.4% (-26.6 to 34.7)), whereas ASMR changed by -17.5% (-36.2 to 13.4). All cervical cancer DALYs were attributable to human papillomavirus infection, with tobacco use contributing 5.9% (3.2-9.3) globally. By 2050, global ASIR and ASMR are forecast to change by -12.5% (-25.7 to 3.5) and -9.0% (-21.5 to 6.6) from 2024, yet absolute cases and deaths are forecast to rise by 20.2% (4.6-38.5) and 39.3% (23.6-57.3). ASIR and ASMR are forecast to remain highest in low-income countries. Intensified action is needed to accelerate progress.

title: Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in ISCHEMIA-EXTEND.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: It is unknown whether routine invasive management of chronic coronary disease improves long-term survival when added to guideline-directed medical therapy. OBJECTIVE: To compare the effects of initial invasive and conservative strategies on long-term mortality in patients with chronic coronary disease. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this long-term follow-up study of the International Study of Comparative Health Effectiveness with Medical and Invasive Approaches (ISCHEMIA), an international trial of patients with chronic coronary disease, moderate or severe ischemia, left ventricular ejection fraction of 35% or more, and no left main coronary artery disease, unacceptable angina, or recent acute coronary syndrome, participants were randomized at 320 sites in 37 countries beginning August 2012 and followed up through December 2025. Data were analyzed using the intention-to-treat principle. INTERVENTION: ISCHEMIA randomized patients to an initial invasive strategy of guideline-directed medical therapy plus coronary angiography and revascularization (when feasible) or an initial conservative strategy with guideline-directed medical therapy alone, with invasive management for failure of medical therapy. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: All-cause, cardiovascular, and noncardiovascular mortality were analyzed using cumulative incidence estimates, Cox and Fine-Gray models, bayesian analysis, and restricted mean survival time. RESULTS: Among 5179 participants, median age was 64 (IQR, 58-70) years; 23% were female, 42% had diabetes, and median ejection fraction was 60% (IQR, 55%-65%). During 9-year median follow-up (range, 1 day to 13.4 years), 1071 deaths occurred (782 during extended follow-up): 672 cardiovascular, 359 noncardiovascular, and 40 unclassified. All-cause 11-year mortality was not significantly different between groups (25.8% invasive vs 26.9% conservative; estimated difference, -1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -4.2 to 2.1 percentage points]; adjusted hazard ratio [AHR], 0.97 [95% CI, 0.86-1.09]). By bayesian analysis, the posterior probability of more than 1 percentage-point survival benefit to invasive vs conservative was low (18%). Cardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 15.8% in the invasive group vs 17.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, -1.4 percentage points [95% CI, -4.0 to 1.3 percentage points]; AHR, 0.88 [95% CI, 0.75-1.02]). Noncardiovascular mortality at 11 years was 9.1% in the invasive group vs 8.1% in the conservative group (estimated difference, 1.0 percentage point [95% CI, -0.9 to 2.9 percentage points]; AHR, 1.18 [95% CI, 0.96-1.45]). Eleven-year restricted mean survival was not significantly different (estimated difference, 14 days [95% CI, -41 to 70 days]). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, long-term all-cause mortality in patients with high-risk chronic coronary disease was not significantly different after routine invasive vs initial conservative management. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04894877.

title: Midlife Metabolic Syndrome as Mediator Between Early-Life Insulin Resistance and Later-Life Cardiovascular Diseases.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome framework describes progression from early metabolic dysfunction to clinical cardiovascular disease. Insulin resistance (IR) in young adulthood may contribute to later atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), but the extent to which this association is mediated through midlife metabolic syndrome (MetS) remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: We aimed to evaluate the association between young-adulthood IR and later-life ASCVD and quantify mediation through midlife MetS. METHODS: We analyzed 3,622 Black and White participants in the Coronary Artery Risk Development in Young Adults study who were aged 18 to 30 years at baseline and free of ASCVD through year 20. IR was defined as a Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance value at or above the 75th percentile (≥2.67). MetS was assessed at year 20, and ASCVD events were ascertained through year 35. Parametric g-computation with pooled logistic regression estimated total and mediated effects on cumulative ASCVD risk at the end of follow-up, accounting for midlife lifestyle factors as exposure-induced mediator-outcome confounders. RESULTS: At baseline, 907 of 3,622 participants (25%) had IR. During a median follow-up of 14 years (Q1-Q3: 14-14 years) after year 20, 143 of 3,622 (3.9%) participants experienced an ASCVD event. Young-adulthood IR was associated with a 1.50-fold higher ASCVD risk at the end of follow-up (95% CI: 1.13-2.01), with 63.4% of the association mediated through midlife MetS (indirect risk ratio: 1.29; 95% CI: 1.13-1.48). CONCLUSIONS: Young-adulthood IR was associated with higher later-life ASCVD risk, with a substantial proportion mediated through midlife MetS. These findings suggest early identification of IR and prevention of progression to MetS may help reduce long-term cardiovascular risk.

title: Thymectomy Extent, Immune Recovery, and Infectious Burden After Neonatal Cardiac Surgery.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Neonatal cardiac surgery frequently requires thymectomy, but the consequences of extensive thymic removal remain uncertain. METHODS: We retrospectively studied 105 neonates undergoing sternotomy (2015-2024), comparing infections and 6-month lymphocyte recovery after partial versus total thymectomy, with Firth regression adjusted for bypass duration and surgical era. Separate cohorts underwent paired plasma biomarker (n=8) and whole-blood RNA sequencing (n=4) analysis before and after thymectomy. RESULTS: Among 105 neonates, 27 underwent partial and 78 total thymectomy. Multiple infections occurred in 2 of 27 (7%) after partial and 23 of 78 (30%) after total thymectomy (P=0.02); after adjustment for bypass duration and surgical era, the association was not statistically significant (Firth-adjusted odds ratio, 2.99 [95% CI, 0.82-15.85]; P=0.10). Median lymphocyte count decreased after total but increased after partial thymectomy (change, -0.8 versus +0.9×103/μL; P=0.011). Tumor necrosis factor-α decreased in all 8 biomarker participants (unadjusted P=0.0078). RNA sequencing in 4 patients (2 partial, 2 total thymectomy) identified 835 differentially expressed genes; pre-T-cell receptor α decreased in all 4 pairs (log2 fold change, -2.50; adjusted P=6×10-6). CONCLUSIONS: Total thymectomy was associated with reduced 6-month lymphocyte recovery and higher unadjusted odds of multiple infections. The infection association was not statistically significant after adjustment, and few events (2 of 27 after partial thymectomy) limit precision and cannot exclude a clinically important effect; these findings are hypothesis-generating. Biomarker and transcriptomic findings are exploratory and cannot distinguish thymectomy from surgery, maturation, or postoperative recovery. Prospective studies are underway to evaluate thymic preservation and autologous reimplantation.

title: Behavior-Based Electrogram Mapping Identifies Potential Functional Substrates in Atrial Fibrillation: The KSP-AF Randomized Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Conventional substrate mapping during atrial fibrillation (AF) may fail to capture dynamic electrogram behavior. Key spatiotemporal potentials (KSPs) are electrogram patterns identified by their temporal behavior during AF. We evaluated whether KSP-guided ablation improves outcomes beyond pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) and characterized their short-term frequency consistency. METHODS: In this single-center randomized study, 100 patients with paroxysmal or persistent AF undergoing first-time ablation were assigned to PVI plus KSP-guided ablation or PVI alone. The primary endpoint was 24-month single-procedure freedom from documented AF recurrence without antiarrhythmic drugs. Dominant frequency (DF) analysis included 93 KSP regions from 18 patients, assessed across four consecutive 5-second epochs. RESULTS: Acute AF termination occurred in 68% of patients with PVI + KSP versus 26% with PVI alone (P < 0.001). At 24 months, freedom from AF recurrence was 74% versus 48% (HR 0.38, 95% CI 0.18-0.79; P = 0.010), and freedom from AF/atrial tachycardia recurrence was 68% versus 46% (HR 0.49, 95% CI 0.25-0.97; P = 0.040). Within-recording temporal DF variability was low (coefficient of variation, 4.8 ± 1.2%). CONCLUSION: Adding KSP-guided ablation to PVI improved acute and 24-month rhythm outcomes in this single-center trial. These findings support further evaluation of behavior-based mapping to identify potential functional AF substrates and require multicenter confirmation.

title: Exercise exposure and arrhythmic patterns in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Exercise is associated with ventricular arrhythmias (VA) in arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC), but relationships with atrial fibrillation (AF) and arrhythmic patterns are less established. OBJECTIVE: To assess prior exercise intensity and dose in relation to AF, VA, and combined arrhythmic patterns across the ARVC diagnostic spectrum. METHODS: Genotype-positive probands and relatives were included. Exercise during the three years preceding diagnosis was assessed retrospectively by structured interview. Intensity was defined by the primary activity's Metabolic Equivalent of Task (MET) and dose as MET-hours/week across activities. AF and VA were assessed at first visit and last follow-up. RESULTS: We included 122 individuals (49% women; mean age 39±17 years), with a median follow-up of 13.5 years. AF prevalence increased from 5% to 21% and VA from 26% to 37%. Median onset ages were 55 years for AF and 36 years for VA. Both exercise measures were associated with VA at both time points. Exercise dose was associated with AF at first visit and intensity at last follow-up. Median exercise dose increased across groups with no arrhythmia, AF only, VA only, and both. The association between AF and VA at last follow-up was attenuated after adjustment for exercise intensity (adjusted OR 2.43, 95% CI 0.85-6.97, p=0.10). CONCLUSIONS: Associations with exercise was consistently associated with VA, but varied for AF by measure and time point. The graded distribution does not establish thresholds or sequential progression. Co-occurrence may reflect shared exercise history, disease susceptibility, and differential surveillance rather than a direct relationship.

title: In familial hypercholesterolaemia, remnant cholesterol above 1 mmol/L is associated with 50% higher risk of coronary artery disease.
abstract: AIMS: Familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH) leads to lifelong elevated low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol and increased risk of coronary artery disease. We tested the hypothesis that elevated remnant cholesterol additionally increases cardiovascular risk in FH. METHODS: In the Copenhagen General Population Study (CGPS) and UK Biobank, 108,751 and 428,625 individuals were classified as with or without FH according to clinical scores and genetic mutations. In the two cohorts, 7,708 and 50,997 experienced coronary artery disease, respectively. RESULTS: In CGPS and UK Biobank, remnant cholesterol ≥1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) was observed in 12% and 11% of individuals without FH (N = 104,226 and 403,172), in 33% and 40% with Simon Broome FH (N = 3,923 and 23,860), in 44% and 78% with MEDPED FH (N = 1,005 and 2,465), in 33% and 34% with DLCN FH (N = 744 and 1,207), and in 12% and 21% of individuals with genetic FH (N = 188 and 875). Likewise in the CGPS and UK Biobank, the multivariable adjusted hazard ratios for coronary artery disease by remnant cholesterol ≥1 vs. < 1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) were 1.49 (95% CI: 1.39-1.59) and 1.47 (1.43-1.52) in individuals without FH, 1.59 (1.31-1.93) and 1.18 (1.10-1.27) in Simon Broome FH, 1.50 (1.08-2.08) and 1.14 (0.89-1.45) in MEDPED FH, 1.60 (1.17-2.21) and 1.59 (1.20-2.09) in DLCN FH, and 1.48 (0.59-3.69) and 1.39 (0.88-2.19) in genetic FH. CONCLUSION: In familial hypercholesterolaemia, remnant cholesterol ≥1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) vs below is associated with ≈50% higher risk of coronary artery disease, that is, above the already high risk due to lifelong genetically elevated LDL cholesterol.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: The SIMPLAAFY Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Following a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) procedure, antithrombotic therapy is administered to safely allow time for device endothelialization. However, the optimal postimplant antithrombotic regimen is unknown. OBJECTIVE: To determine if either reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) or aspirin alone are noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for the composite clinical end point of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding through 6 months post LAAC. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This open-label, 3-group, multicenter clinical trial randomized 1857 patients between October 2024 and December 2025 at 87 US investigational sites, with the final 6-month follow-up in July 2026. Enrolled patients had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, underwent successful LAAC, and were eligible for all 3 regimens. INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly allocated 1:1:1 to DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613). MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the 6-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding. Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (α = .025). Bleeding and 45-day device-related thrombus rates were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment. RESULTS: The cohort had a mean age of 76 (SD, 8) years, 42.9% were female, the mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.2 (SD, 1.3), and 68.0% had paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The primary outcome occurred in 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with a reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, -1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, -3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, -0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria (P < .001 for noninferiority for both). Major bleeding was 4.5% with DAPT, 2.7% with reduced-dose NOACs, and 1.7% with aspirin alone; clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 8.7%, 4.8%, and 3.8%, respectively. Device-related thrombus was observed in 3.4%, 0.9%, and 2.7%, respectively. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Both reduced-dose NOACs and aspirin alone were noninferior to DAPT for 6-month outcomes after uncomplicated LAAC. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06521463.

title: PCSK9-Targeting Therapies and Mortality: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
abstract: AIMS: To evaluate the association of PCSK9-targeting therapies with mortality and cardiovascular events in stable or clinically stabilized randomized trial populations. METHODS: We systematically reviewed randomized trials comparing alirocumab, evolocumab or inclisiran with placebo or active control. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261395609). Treatment effects were pooled as incidence rate ratios (IRRs) using random-effects models. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Prespecified subgroup analyses were based on trial-level known atherosclerosis status, as defined by enrollment criteria. RESULTS: Thirty-two trials enrolled 77,178 participants. Individual atherosclerosis status could not be determined beyond trial-level eligibility criteria. Mortality estimates were predominantly informed by large cardiovascular outcome trials. All-cause mortality was lower with PCSK9-targeting therapy (IRR 0.88, 95% CI 0.82-0.95). Estimates favored PCSK9-targeting treatment in both trials requiring known atherosclerosis for enrollment (IRR 0.90, 95% CI 0.83-0.98) and trials without such an enrollment requirement (IRR 0.78, 95% CI 0.62-0.97; interaction p = 0.21). PCSK9-targeting treatment additionally reduced myocardial infarction, stroke, and coronary revascularization rates. Leave-one-out estimates remained directionally consistent. CONCLUSION: PCSK9-targeting therapies were associated with lower all-cause mortality and fewer ischemic events across trial populations. The predominant contribution of large cardiovascular outcome trials enrolling populations with known atherosclerosis and using PCSK9 antibodies limits the ability to infer a survival benefit in populations not selected on the basis of atherosclerosis status and across individual therapies, particularly inclisiran.

title: The Art Behind the Algorithm: Hybrid Ablation and the Need for a Lifetime Strategy in Non-Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation.
abstract: The management of persistent and long-standing persistent atrial fibrillation remains highly variable in clinical practice, despite increasingly refined guidelines and an expanding ablation armamentarium. Treatment sequencing is frequently driven by local program infrastructure and institutional culture, and hybrid ablation is often deferred until multiple endocardial procedures have failed, by which point progressive atrial remodeling may have already narrowed the therapeutic window. Randomized and registry data support a meaningful role for hybrid ablation earlier in the disease course of selected patients with non-paroxysmal AF, particularly those with enlarged atria, prolonged AF duration, advanced substrate, or failed prior endocardial ablation. Contemporary pulsed-field ablation technology has improved procedural safety and efficiency, yet freedom from recurrence at one year in persistent AF remains substantially lower than in paroxysmal AF across all current energy platforms, reflecting the complexity of atrial substrate over time. This ongoing myocardial remodeling places non-paroxysmal AF closer to a chronic structural cardiac disease than to a discrete procedural target and demands a lifetime management strategy rather than a sequence of isolated procedural decisions. The mindset for other progressive structural cardiac diseases has already moved in this direction-aortic valve stenosis is now managed through a multidisciplinary team that integrates anatomy, timing, procedural durability, and long-term risk across the full patient trajectory. We propose an AF Heart Team framework for non-paroxysmal AF in which catheter-based, hybrid, and surgical strategies are selected according to disease phenotype and lifetime trajectory, with the goal of intervening before advanced remodeling reduces the likelihood of durable rhythm control.

title: Urinary Metals, Soluble Urokinase Plasminogen Activator Receptor, and Outcomes in the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Environmental metal exposure is associated with cardiovascular disease (CVD) and mortality, potentially through inflammation. Soluble urokinase plasminogen activator receptor (suPAR), a stable marker of immune activation associated with CVD and death, may capture this pathway. We examined associations of urinary metals with suPAR and whether suPAR-associated components were present in cadmium-outcome associations. METHODS: In the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, we studied 5,148 adults free of clinical CVD (2000-2002). We estimated associations of 11 creatinine-standardized urinary metals with serum suPAR by linear regression (per interquartile-range [IQR] increase), compared associations across suPAR, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and D-dimer, and used VanderWeele 4-way decomposition to estimate suPAR-associated indirect components of cadmium associations with all-cause mortality and four adjudicated cardiovascular outcomes. RESULTS: Of 11 metals, 7 were associated with suPAR; cadmium showed the strongest association (7.99% higher suPAR per IQR; 95% CI, 6.14-9.87) followed by cobalt, copper, molybdenum, tungsten, and zinc, whereas barium was inversely associated. The association was monotonic and persisted among never-smokers (5.54%; 95% CI, 3.03-8.11). Over a median 14.7 years, higher urinary cadmium was associated with all-cause mortality (Q4-vs-Q1 hazard ratio, 1.43; 95% CI, 1.18-1.74); the suPAR-associated proportion was 0.30 (95% CI, 0.13-0.47). CONCLUSIONS: Cadmium showed a larger association with suPAR than with hs-CRP, IL-6, or D-dimer. An exploratory decomposition identified a suPAR-associated component of this association. Findings for cardiovascular outcomes were directionally consistent but not definitive. suPAR-related immune activation is a candidate pathway linking cadmium to mortality, warranting longitudinal and mechanistic confirmation.

title: Targeting ALDOA Lactylation Reverses Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Hypertension by Disrupting Actin Polymerization and YAP Activation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Maladaptive vascular remodeling is a hallmark of pulmonary hypertension (PH), and therapeutic strategies directly targeting the pathological activity of smooth muscle cells remain limited. Metabolic and epigenetic dysregulation are established drivers of PH, and lysine lactylation has emerged as a novel posttranslational modification implicated in diverse diseases; however, its direct contribution to PH progression remains undefined. METHODS: Integrated lactylomic and proteomic profiling was performed in hypoxic human pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells. The functional role of ALDOA (aldolase A) lactylation at lysine 42 (K42) was assessed using site-specific mutant virus and smooth muscle cell-specific inducible ALDOA knockout mice in 2 established PH models: SU5416+hypoxia in mice and monocrotaline in rats. RESULTS: We identified ALDOA as a prominent lactylation target in hypoxic pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells, with K42 lactylation consistently elevated in primary pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cells derived from PH rodent models and human PH tissues. Mechanistically, AARS1 (alanyl-tRNA synthetase 1)-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation enhanced its binding to γ-actin, independent of glycolytic activity. This lactylation-enhanced interaction promoted F-actin polymerization and activated YAP (Yes-associated protein) signaling via LATS1 (large tumor suppressor kinase 1) inhibition, thereby driving pulmonary arterial smooth muscle cell proliferation and phenotypic switching. Moreover, YAP/TEAD4 (TEA domain transcription factor 4)-mediated transcriptional upregulation of AARS1 established a positive feedback loop reinforcing ALDOA K42 lactylation under hypoxia. In vivo, ALDOA inducible knockout or reconstitution with the lactylation-deficient K42R (lysine 42 mutant to arginine) mutant attenuated experimental PH progression, with suppressed F-actin/YAP activation and reduced vascular remodeling. Furthermore, competitive inhibition of lactylation through β‑alanine reduced ALDOA K42 lactylation and ameliorated vascular remodeling in ALDOA-overexpressing rodent PH models. Translationally, pharmacological disruption of the ALDOA/γ-actin interaction by raltegravir suppressed cytoskeletal reorganization and YAP signaling, mitigating PH progression in both mouse and rat models. CONCLUSIONS: AARS1-mediated ALDOA K42 lactylation drives pulmonary vascular remodeling through a mechanism independent of ALDOA's catalytic activity, promoting F-actin polymerization and YAP activation. Precision targeting of this modification selectively inhibits pathological signaling while preserving metabolic homeostasis, highlighting a translational potential for precision intervention in PH.

title: Digital Health Intervention to Optimize Heart Failure Management After Hospital Discharge in Brazil (OPT-HF): A Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Barriers to optimizing guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) for heart failure include infrequent clinical visits, clinician inertia, and poor patient knowledge. Digital health interventions (DHIs) may mitigate these barriers, but evidence from low- and middle-income countries is limited. We evaluated whether a DHI would improve GDMT use and other outcomes in Brazil. METHODS: We enrolled adults admitted for heart failure with ejection fraction <50% and GDMT gaps (≥1 GDMT class not started or ≥2 classes ≤50% target dose) across 5 Brazilian public hospitals from November 2023 to August 2025. Participants were randomized to usual care or the DHI comprising a patient-facing app linked to a provider dashboard, supporting nurse-led remote monitoring, cardiologist teleconsultations, and self-care education. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in mean heart failure GDMT score (0-12) at 90 days. Secondary outcomes included differences in health status, self-care, hospitalization rates, and all-cause mortality. Intention-to-treat analyses used baseline-adjusted linear regression and estimated risk ratios. RESULTS: Among 154 randomized patients (DHI: 87; usual care: 67), mean age was 65±14 years; 62% were male, 66% were Black, 44% had ≤4 years of education, and 68% were New York Heart Association class III/IV. Primary outcome data were available for 141 participants (91.6%; DHI: 81; usual care: 60). Mean GDMT scores increased from 7.2 in both groups to 10.5 with DHI versus 7.5 with usual care at 90 days (changes: +3.3 versus +0.3 points; adjusted difference, 3.01 [95% CI, 2.30-3.73]; P<0.001). A borderline difference was observed in health status (7.89; P=0.052). Improvements were observed in self-care (β=14.79 [95% CI, 9.78-19.81]; P<0.001). Fewer participants were hospitalized with DHI than usual care (9/87 [10.3%] versus 15/67 [22.4%]; risk ratio, 0.46 [95% CI, 0.21-0.99]; P=0.048), with no statistically significant difference for deaths. CONCLUSIONS: In patients hospitalized for heart failure in Brazil, a context-adapted DHI improved GDMT use, self-care, and reduced hospitalizations. These findings provide early randomized evidence supporting DHI for GDMT optimization in low-resource settings. REGISTRATION: URL: https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-10vpf9bm; Unique identifier: U1111-1295-1864.
